skill.name: python-testing-patterns
skill.description: Guide for creating pytest test suites with fixtures, mocking, async tests, database tests, coverage, and CI integration.
skill.summary: Create maintainable Python tests with pytest patterns and practical examples.
skill.author: ActiveInferenceInstitute

security_audit.summary: All static findings were assessed as false positives in the context of a static pytest testing guide. The flagged items are Markdown fences, placeholder URLs, mock HTTP examples, test-only environment values, or ordinary pytest and SQLAlchemy examples. No prompt injection, covert exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Production-like placeholder key names can confuse users and scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Rename placeholder values such as production-key to clearly fake values such as example-key.

remediation.issue: A sample prints a database URL, even though it is a local test placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid teaching logs that print full database URLs; log a safe label instead.

content.value_statement: Python tests often become brittle, slow, or incomplete. This skill guides pytest structure, fixtures, mocks, async tests, coverage, and CI setup.
actual_capabilities: Shows pytest unit test structure with arrange, act, and assert examples.
Demonstrates fixtures, fixture scope, autouse behavior, and teardown patterns.
Explains mocking HTTP clients with unittest.mock and pytest assertions.
Covers async tests, monkeypatch usage, temporary files, and property-based tests.
Provides coverage, CI workflow, pytest.ini, and pyproject.toml examples.
limitations: Examples are instructional and must be adapted to each repository.
It does not run tests or verify project-specific results by itself.
It focuses on pytest and common Python libraries, not every testing framework.
Some examples use placeholder URLs and credentials for teaching only.

use_cases.title: Add Unit Tests to a Python Module
use_cases.description: Create focused pytest cases for functions, classes, edge cases, and expected exceptions.

use_cases.title: Mock External Services Safely
use_cases.description: Replace API calls with mocks and assertions so tests avoid real network requests.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Testing Practices
use_cases.description: Define fixtures, coverage settings, CI workflow steps, and clear test organization.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Pytest Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner test creation for a small module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-testing-patterns to design beginner pytest tests for this module. Include happy paths, edge cases, and exception checks.

prompt_templates.title: Add Fixtures and Parameterization
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate suite cleanup and coverage expansion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply python-testing-patterns to refactor these tests with fixtures and parameterization. Keep each case independent and readable.

prompt_templates.title: Mock APIs and Environment Values
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-testing-patterns to test this API-facing code. Mock network calls and isolate environment variables with monkeypatch.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Complete Test Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a production Python project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-testing-patterns to propose a complete pytest strategy with unit, integration, async, database, coverage, and CI guidance.

output_examples.input: A calculator module needs tests for success and failure cases.
output_examples.output: A pytest plan covering normal arithmetic, division by zero, invalid inputs, and parameterized cases.

output_examples.input: An API client should be tested without calling the real service.
output_examples.output: A mock-based approach that verifies response handling, error handling, call arguments, and no live network dependency.

output_examples.input: A team wants repeatable test quality in CI.
output_examples.output: A testing checklist with fixtures, coverage thresholds, marker usage, and workflow steps for every pull request.

best_practices: Keep tests isolated, deterministic, and explicit about their setup.
Mock external dependencies and assert important calls or side effects.
Measure coverage while prioritizing meaningful behavior checks.
anti_patterns: Do not write vague tests that only prove code executes.
Do not depend on real services, local state, or shared test order.
Do not chase coverage numbers without testing important behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests for me?
faq.answer: No. It guides test design and examples; the agent or user must run project tests.

faq.question: Which test framework does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on pytest with common helpers like unittest.mock, pytest-asyncio, hypothesis, and pytest-cov.

faq.question: Can it help with API testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to mock requests and verify behavior without live network calls.

faq.question: Can it test async Python code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes pytest-asyncio patterns for async functions, concurrent tasks, and async fixtures.

faq.question: Does it include CI guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes coverage commands and a GitHub Actions testing workflow example.

faq.question: Are the URLs and keys real secrets?
faq.answer: No. They are placeholder values used in educational examples.
